subject: Risk & Compliance
title: Why White-Collar Sentences Are Light
description: A quick, practical guide to Why White-Collar Sentences Are Light.

hook.text: A drug dealer gets 15 years. An executive who stole $100 million gets 3 years at a minimum-security camp.

buildup.text: White-collar criminals often receive lighter sentences because they are seen as non-violent first offenders.

discovery.text: Sentencing guidelines consider loss amount but judges have wide discretion. Good lawyers reduce time dramatically.

twist.text: Federal white-collar inmates often serve time in 'Club Fed' — minimum-security facilities with tennis courts.

climax.text: Light sentences for massive financial damage undermine public trust that the justice system is fair.

punchline.text: Steal millions in a suit. Get a lighter sentence. Every time.

quiz.question: Why do white-collar criminals often get lighter sentences?
options: They're seen as non-violent first offenders with good lawyers
Their crimes cause less total damage
Judges are not allowed to give long sentences
